title: Same Study Time, Different Result
hook: Two students. Same total study time: two hours and twenty minutes. One spreads it over a week. The other crams it the night before.

segments.n: On test day, both feel ready. The crammer often feels more confident, because everything is still fresh.
segments.p: A classroom with two desks and test papers, Hiro smiling calmly, the cap figure giving a big confident thumbs up, a small checkmark badge above the cap figure colored amber-orange. segments.n: But weeks later, the spread-out student usually remembers more. Researchers have studied this spacing effect for over a century.
segments.p: A calendar with four pages flipped, Hiro holding a thick glowing notebook colored amber-orange and smiling, the cap figure scratching his head over an empty notebook. Hiro, the same character as the reference, with a tiny black mole under the eye on the right side of the image; the second figure with a small cap has a plain face and no mole. segments.n: Researchers think that each time you almost forget and then recall something, your brain strengthens that memory.

segments.n: Cramming skips that step. Everything is learned in one block, so it tends to fade faster.
segments.p: A single tall column of books collapsing with small pieces falling away and a fading dotted outline, the cap figure looking up at it, the falling pieces colored amber-orange. Hiro, the same character as the reference, with a tiny black mole under the eye on the right side of the image; the second figure with a small cap has a plain face and no mole. segments.n: So split your study across days. Twenty minutes a day can beat one huge night. Which student are you this week?
